topic: The stamen and the four-chambered anther
title: The Stamen and the Four-Chambered Anther
summary: Touch a lily and your finger turns orange. Where is that pollen made? Inside the stamen, in an anther with four chambers.

notes.title: 01 – The Stamen and the Four-Chambered Anther

keyPoints: A **stamen** has a long, thin **filament** and an **anther** at the top.
A typical anther has **2 lobes** with 2 chambers each: **4 microsporangia**.
The microsporangium wall has **4 layers**: epidermis, endothecium, middle layers and tapetum.
The innermost **tapetum** nourishes the developing pollen grains.
The **sporogenous tissue** in the centre gives rise to pollen grains.

sections.h: The wall of a microsporangium, outside to inside

quiz.q: A typical anther has how many microsporangia?
Which layer nourishes the developing pollen?
quiz.explain: The tapetum is the innermost layer.
